title: Poland, 1939: five dates, different kinds of change
subtitle: An introduction to the first Ostfront Atlas timeline
author: R.G. Cruise
body:
## Reading the dates

On 23 August 1939, Germany and the Soviet Union signed the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact. Its secret protocol assigned spheres of influence in eastern Europe, including plans to divide Poland.[1]

Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. The Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September. These were military invasions, not changes in recognized Polish sovereignty.[2]

On 28 September, Germany and the Soviet Union signed the Boundary and Friendship Treaty, revising their territorial arrangements in occupied Poland.[3] A treaty date does not establish that a military line or civil administration changed everywhere at once.

On 26 October, German annexations and the civilian General Government marked a further administrative stage in German-occupied territory.[4] The atlas treats invasion, military control, annexation, and occupation administration as distinct events. It does not yet draw historical boundaries for any of these dates.

## References

1. United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, *German-Soviet Pact*.
2. United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, *Invasion of Poland, Fall 1939*.
3. U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1939, Volume I*, chapter on the 28 September treaty.
4. United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, *1939: Key Dates*.
